entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
entry.summary:
We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games. First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #algebra-geometry #optimization

entry.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$.
entry.summary:
We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #probability-stats #logic

entry.title: Lattice moments and quantum designs
entry.summary:
We show that the ensemble of unimodular Gottesman$-$Kitaev$-$Preskill distributions fails to form a rigged quantum $3$-design and quantify the replica defect that determines this failure. This is established by rederiving a second moment formula for symplectic lattices in a self-contained manner.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #quantum-computing #post-quantum

entry.title: Just How Secure is SRP, Really?
entry.summary:
An asymmetric Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) protocol allows a client and a server to agree upon a cryptographic key, with the only information shared in advance being a low-entropy password (memorized by the client) and a corresponding password file (stored in the server). The standard security definition for aPAKE is in the Universally Composable (UC) framework. Since aPAKE does not rely on a PKI, such protocols have received much attention in recent years due to their potential of replacing the traditional “password-over-TLS” approach for client-server authentication on the Internet.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Highly Efficient and Round-Optimal Asymmetric PAKE
entry.summary:
An asymmetric Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) protocol allows a client, who holds a raw password, and a server, who holds a one-way mapping of the password, to jointly establish a cryptographically strong session key, without an authenticated channel. The standard security definition for aPAKE is in the Universal Composability (UC) framework. Despite its great potential of being used in practice, existing aPAKE protocols are either not round-optimal, computationally inefficient, or not proven secure.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Structural Change in the Multilayer World Trade Web: An Economic Dominance Theory Approach
entry.summary:
Most studies of the World Trade Web (WTW) describe its topology: degrees, strengths, centralities, communities, or the similarity between product networks and years. This paper presents Economic Dominance Theory (EDT), initiated by Lantner (1974), and positions it as an alternative theory of structural dependence in directed flow networks rather than an additional toolbox. EDT normalizes bilateral flows into a Ghosh matrix of directed propagation and measures circular interdependence through its determinant, which aggregates the feedback circuits by which influence returns to its origin.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #combinatorics #clean-tech
